summary: Durable idempotency with Redis requires architect (data contract and store design), scrum_master (split into store, runner, worker and test stories), designer (file plan for each), test_architect (edge cases for concurrency and TTL), and critic (ensure contract consistency across specs).

steps.why: Extract the idempotency contract, store API, runner changes and worker changes into structured requirements for architecture review.
Design the Redis key contract, claim/complete/release atomicity guarantees, error handling strategy and the two-store abstraction before implementation.
Split into separate stories for the store component, runner integration, worker status logic and tests so each can be implemented and reviewed independently.
Each story needs a concrete file plan: the store module structure, where claim/complete/release calls go in runner.py, the conditional status write in orders.py, and test file organization.
Pin edge cases as tests: concurrent claims, TTL expiry, Redis failure modes, resume path without claim, and the worker status write guard.
Cross-check that the HLD contract, breakdown stories, LLD file plans and test cases all agree on key format, claim semantics, TTL values and error handling.
Pack per-ticket specs into merged_plan.md for review.
Human approval of specs and this plan before Dev.

skipped.why: Scope is clear from the ticket: durable idempotency with Redis, no product ambiguity or user-facing decision.
